b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Drip Campaign: A series of pre-written emails or texts that send on a schedule after someone joins a list or takes an action. A drip campaign is a pre-written series of emails, or sometimes text messages, sent automatically over time. Each message is released on a schedule or after a trigger, such as someone joining your list, booking an appointment, or downloading a guide. The name comes from the way messages arrive steadily, a little at a time, instead of all at once. Common examples include welcome series, onboarding sequences, appointment reminders, review requests, and re-engagement campaigns. Why Drip Campaign Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Small businesses rarely have time to send personal follow-up messages to every contact. A drip campaign lets a Mishawaka med spa welcome every new subscriber, a Goshen accountant remind clients about tax deadlines, and a Warsaw contractor request reviews after each job, all automatically. Because each drip campaign is built once and runs continuously, it delivers consistent communication that keeps your business top of mind and turns one-time contacts into repeat customers. Choose a trigger A signup, purchase, appointment, form submission, or date starts the sequence. Plan the messages Map each email's purpose, from welcome to education to offer. Measure and refine Track opens, clicks, replies, and conversions for each message. A South Bend dog groomer creates three drip campaigns. New clients receive a welcome series with grooming tips and booking reminders. Every client receives a reminder email six weeks after an appointment, the typical time between grooms. Clients who have not booked in four months receive a friendly check-in with a seasonal offer. The reminder campaign alone fills more of the schedule each month, and the owner spends less time on phone follow-ups. Getting Started With Drip Campaign Begin with the drip campaign that matches your most common customer moment. For most local businesses, that is a welcome series for new subscribers or a follow-up sequence after a service. Write three to five short messages, each with one purpose and one clear call to action . Set them up in your email platform with sensible spacing, test every link, and send yourself a test run. Trust sits at the center, supported by the other three. E-E-A-T is not a single score or setting. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Google Business Profile: Your free listing on Google Search and Google Maps. It shows your hours, phone number, photos, services, and customer reviews. What Is Google Business Profile? A Google Business Profile is the free listing Google shows when someone searches for your business by name or looks for a service near them. It holds the details a customer needs to choose you: your name, hours, phone number, website, address or service area, photos, services, products, posts, and reviews. It appears on Google Search, in the map pack, and inside Google Maps. For most local businesses, the profile is the first impression. Many customers read your reviews, check your hours, look at photos, and tap to call without ever visiting your website. That makes the profile a working storefront, and Google treats it as one of the strongest signals for where you show up in local results. Why Google Business Profile Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses In towns like Goshen, Elkhart , Warsaw, and South Bend , people search with a location in mind: "plumber near me," "best pizza in Mishawaka ," "dentist open Saturday." Google answers those searches with profiles, and the businesses with complete, active, well-reviewed profiles earn the clicks and calls. A strong profile also feeds AI tools. Google AI Overviews , Gemini, and other assistants pull business facts from profiles and reviews, so accurate categories, services, and hours help AI describe your business correctly when customers ask for recommendations. How Google Business Profile Works Claim and verify Google confirms you own the business, usually through a postcard, phone, email, or video check. Fill in every field Primary category, secondary categories, services, hours, attributes, description, and service area all tell Google which searches you fit. Earn and answer reviews Review count, rating, recency, and your replies shape both rankings and trust. Stay active Photos, posts, product updates, and answered questions show Google and customers that the business is open and engaged. Measure results The Performance tab shows searches, calls, direction requests, and website clicks so you see what the profile produces. A family HVAC company in Elkhart County switches its primary category from "Contractor" to "HVAC Contractor," adds furnace repair, AC installation, and duct cleaning as services, uploads job photos every week, and asks every happy customer for a review with a short link. Within a few months the company appears in the map pack for "furnace repair Goshen " and calls from the profile climb, which the owner tracks in the Performance tab. Getting Started With Google Business Profile Start by searching your business name on Google and Google Maps. If a profile appears, select "Own this business?" to claim it. If none appears, create one at business.google.com using your exact business name, the category that best describes your main service, and your phone number and website. Once verified, set aside an hour to complete every section. Write a description that explains who you serve and which towns you cover, such as Elkhart, Goshen, and Middlebury . Add at least ten real photos, including your team, your work, your vehicles, and your location. Then build a simple weekly habit: one new photo or post, a reply to every new review, and a quick check of your hours. Small, steady activity adds up faster than a single big update once a year. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Google Search Console: A free Google tool that shows which searches bring people to your site, how often your pages appear, and which pages Google has stored. It reports the searches that show your pages, how many clicks and impressions each page earns, and whether Google can crawl and index your site. It also alerts you to problems such as indexing errors, mobile usability issues, Core Web Vitals scores, security issues, and manual actions. Because it is free and comes directly from Google, it is one of the most valuable tools for any Northern Indiana business investing in SEO. It also gives you proof. When you update a page or publish new content, Search Console shows whether impressions and clicks actually grew, so you can see which efforts pay off and explain results to partners or staff with real numbers instead of impressions. t: What Is an Internal Link? How Linking Your Pages Helps SEO
d: Internal links connect pages on your own website. Learn how they guide visitors, spread authority, and help Google understand your services and service areas.
h: Internal Link Links between your own pages that guide visitors and search engines | What Is Internal Link? | Why Internal Link Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses | How Internal Link Works | A Local Example | Getting Started With Internal Link | Quick Wins to Improve Your Internal Linking | What to Watch For | Internal Link FAQ
b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Internal Link: A link from one page on your website to another page on the same website. Internal links guide visitors to helpful pages and show search engines how your content connects. An internal link is a link from one page on your website to another page on the same site. Navigation menus, footer links, buttons, and links inside paragraphs are all internal links. Internal links do three jobs at once. They help visitors find related information, they help search engines discover and understand your pages, and they pass authority from strong pages to the pages you most want to rank. Why Internal Link Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Many local business websites have great service pages that search engines rarely visit because nothing links to them. An Elkhart County roofer whose blog post on hail damage links directly to its "Storm Damage Roof Repair" page sends both readers and ranking signals where they matter most. Internal links also tell a clear story about your expertise. Linking related services, town pages, and helpful guides together shows Google and AI tools that your business covers a topic thoroughly across Northern Indiana and Michiana . Discovery Search engines follow links to find new and updated pages. Context The linked words, called anchor text , describe the page being linked. Authority flow Pages with strong rankings or backlinks share value with the pages they link to. Structure Linking patterns show which pages are most important and how topics relate. Visitor paths Clear links move readers from questions to services to contact. A Valparaiso landscaping company publishes a guide to spring lawn care. It adds links inside the article to its lawn aeration, fertilization, and landscape design service pages, plus its Porter County service area page. Each service page links back to related guides. The service pages begin ranking higher, and visitors who arrive on the guide more often request a quote. Getting Started With Internal Link List your most important pages: the services that bring in the most revenue and the towns you most want to serve. Then search your site for articles, FAQs, and other pages that mention those topics without linking to them. Each mention is a ready-made internal link opportunity. Add links using descriptive words such as "furnace repair in Goshen " rather than "click here." Make sure every important page receives links from several related pages and is reachable within a few clicks from the homepage. Repeat the review whenever you publish new content so each new page connects to the rest of your site right away. Quick Wins to Improve Your Internal Linking Link every blog post to at least one related service page Use descriptive anchor text that names the destination topic Link service pages to the towns and counties you serve Add related links at the end of articles and service pages Fix or remove links to pages that no longer exist Orphan pages. Pages with no internal links are hard for search engines and visitors to find. Generic anchors. "Click here" tells search engines nothing about the destination. Broken links. Update links after changing URLs so visitors never hit dead ends. Relevance. Link where it genuinely helps the reader take the next step. How many internal links should a page have? There is no fixed number. Add links wherever they help readers, and make sure every important page receives several relevant links. Do footer and menu links count? Yes. They help discovery, while links inside the main content carry stronger context about the destination. Are internal links as valuable as backlinks? They work differently. Backlinks bring authority from outside, and internal links share and direct that authority within your site. Should I link to the same page more than once? One clear link per page is usually enough; repeated links add little extra value. Want your website working as one connected system?

t: What Is Lead Nurturing? Turning Interested Leads Into Customers
d: Lead nurturing builds relationships with leads who are not ready to buy yet, through helpful emails, texts, and content. Learn how local businesses nurture leads.
h: Lead Nurturing Helping interested people become ready-to-buy customers | What Is Lead Nurturing? | Why Lead Nurturing Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses | How Lead Nurturing Works | A Local Example | Getting Started With Lead Nurturing | Quick Wins to Improve Your Lead Nurturing | What to Watch For | Lead Nurturing FAQ
b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Lead Nurturing: Building trust with leads through helpful follow-up until they are ready to buy. Lead nurturing is the process of staying in helpful contact with people who have shown interest in your business but are not ready to buy yet. It uses emails, text messages, retargeting ads, and useful content to answer questions, build trust, and guide each lead toward a decision. Good nurturing feels like service, not pressure. Each message gives the lead something useful, such as a guide, a cost explanation, a customer story, or a timely reminder, while making the next step easy when they are ready. Why Lead Nurturing Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Many local purchases take time. A Granger family planning a basement finish, a Goshen manufacturer comparing payroll providers, or an Elkhart couple shopping for a wedding venue may take weeks or months to decide. Businesses that stay helpful during that time are the ones chosen in the end. Nurturing also makes marketing spend more efficient. Leads you already paid to attract keep producing value, instead of disappearing after one unanswered call or email. Capture the lead A form, call, or download adds the person to your CRM with their interest noted. Segment by need Group leads by service, timeline, or stage so messages fit. Send helpful content Share answers, examples, and stories that address common questions and concerns. Watch for buying signals Pricing page visits, replies, and repeat opens show growing interest. Hand off at the right time Sales follows up personally when a lead is ready. A Middlebury custom home builder receives many inquiries from families who plan to build in a year or two. Instead of a single follow-up call, it creates a nurture sequence: a guide to building costs in Elkhart County , a lot selection checklist, a video tour of a finished home, and a story from a family who recently moved in. Each email invites a planning conversation. Over the following year, a steady share of those early inquiries book design consultations, and the builder's sales team spends its time with families who are already familiar and confident. Getting Started With Lead Nurturing List the questions people ask before choosing you: cost, timing, process, financing, and how you compare to alternatives. Each question can become one helpful email, text, or article in your nurture sequence. Next, set up a simple sequence in your email platform or CRM, such as HubSpot , with four to six messages spaced over several weeks. Add a clear next step in each message, track opens, clicks, and replies, and alert your team when a lead takes a high-intent action. Review the results every quarter and refresh messages that underperform. Quick Wins to Improve Your Lead Nurturing Follow up with every new lead within one business day Send a helpful sequence to leads who are not ready yet Answer cost and timeline questions directly Share real customer stories from your area Alert sales when a lead shows buying signals Too many messages. Space messages so each one feels welcome. Generic content. Messages tailored to the lead's interest perform far better. Missing handoff. Make sure engaged leads reach a real person quickly. Permission. Send marketing emails and texts only with proper consent. How long should lead nurturing last? As long as your typical buying cycle. Quick services may need a few weeks, while large projects may need many months. Is lead nurturing only email? No. Email is common, and nurturing can also include text messages, retargeting ads, phone calls, and direct mail. What is the difference between nurturing and a drip campaign? A drip campaign is one tool for nurturing. Nurturing is the overall strategy of building the relationship. Many local businesses use their email platform or a CRM such as HubSpot to automate sequences and track engagement. Want every lead followed up with care until they are ready to buy? Riley

t: What Is Lead Scoring? Prioritizing Your Best Leads
d: Lead scoring assigns points to leads based on fit and behavior so your team follows up with the most promising prospects first. Learn how to build a simple model.
h: Lead Scoring Ranking leads by fit and interest so your team calls the best first | What Is Lead Scoring? | Why Lead Scoring Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses | How Lead Scoring Works | A Local Example | Getting Started With Lead Scoring | Quick Wins to Improve Your Lead Scoring | What to Watch For | Lead Scoring FAQ
b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Lead Scoring: A points system that ranks leads by how well they fit your business and how engaged they are, so your team calls the warmest leads first. Lead scoring is a system that assigns points to each lead based on how well they fit your ideal customer and how engaged they are with your business. The total score helps your team decide who to contact first and who needs more nurturing. Scores usually combine two types of information. Fit data includes details such as location, company size, industry, or project type. Behavior data includes actions such as visiting the pricing page, opening emails, booking a call, or requesting a quote. CRMs such as HubSpot can calculate scores automatically. Why Lead Scoring Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Small teams have limited time for follow-up. An Elkhart County commercial cleaning company receiving forty inquiries a month benefits from knowing which ones are large, nearby offices ready to sign and which are early researchers. Lead scoring also aligns marketing and sales. Everyone agrees on what a qualified lead looks like, so marketing focuses on attracting more of them and sales spends time where it counts. Define your ideal customer List the traits of your best customers, such as location, size, and service need. Assign fit points Add points for strong-fit traits and subtract for poor fit. Assign behavior points Add points for high-intent actions such as pricing page views or quote requests. Set thresholds Decide what score makes a lead ready for sales. Review and adjust Compare scores with actual sales and refine the model. A Goshen commercial HVAC contractor sets up lead scoring in HubSpot. Leads earn points for being within its Elkhart and St. Joseph county service area, for managing commercial buildings, for visiting the maintenance contract page, and for requesting a site visit. Leads above the threshold go straight to the owner for a same-day call. Lower-scoring leads receive a helpful email sequence about preventive maintenance. Several of them later return, visit the contract page, and cross the threshold, at which point the owner calls them. Getting Started With Lead Scoring Look at your last twenty customers and note what they had in common: location, business type, project size, and the actions they took before buying. Those patterns become the foundation of your scoring model. Start simple, with five to ten criteria and round point values. Set one threshold for "sales ready" leads and route those to immediate follow-up. After two or three months, compare scores with closed deals, raise points for signals that predicted sales, and lower points for those that did not. Quick Wins to Improve Your Lead Scoring Base criteria on your actual best customers Give high points to quote requests and pricing page visits Subtract points for locations outside your service area Route high scores to immediate follow-up Review the model against closed deals each quarter Overcomplication. Too many criteria make scores hard to trust; start small. Stale scores. Reduce points over time for leads who go quiet. Sales feedback. Ask your team which leads were truly ready and adjust. Data quality. Scores depend on accurate form data and tracking. Do small businesses need lead scoring? Any business with more leads than it can follow up on quickly benefits from a simple scoring system. Can HubSpot score leads automatically? Yes. HubSpot offers lead scoring tools, with options depending on your subscription level. What is a good lead score? Scores are relative to your model. What matters is the threshold where leads become likely to buy. How is lead scoring different from lead nurturing? Scoring decides who is ready. Nurturing helps leads who are not ready yet move closer to buying. Want your team spending time on the leads most likely to buy? Riley will build a lead scoring model inside your CRM.

t: What Is llms.txt? A Guide File for AI Tools

b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary llms.txt: A plain text file in Markdown, placed at yoursite.com/llms.txt, that gives AI tools a short, organized guide to your business and your most useful pages. It is an emerging, voluntary standard, and adoption varies among AI providers, so it works best alongside clear, helpful content. llms.txt is a proposed standard for a simple text file, written in Markdown, placed at the root of a website, such as favze.com/llms.txt. It gives large language models a short, organized summary of who you are and links to your most important pages. The idea was introduced in 2024 as a way to help AI tools find the most useful content on a site without sorting through menus, scripts, and layout code. It complements robots.txt , which sets crawling rules, and sitemap .xml, which lists every page. Why llms.txt Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses AI assistants increasingly answer questions about local businesses. A clear llms.txt file gives a Goshen law firm or an Elkhart HVAC company one tidy place that states its services, service areas, and key pages in plain language. It is an inexpensive, low-risk addition. Major AI companies have not confirmed that they rely on llms.txt, so it works best as one part of a broader AI visibility strategy built on clear content, structured data , and consistent business information. Title and summary The file opens with your business name and a one-paragraph description. Organized sections Headings group links to services, locations, resources, and contact pages. Short link descriptions Each link includes a brief note about what the page covers. Plain Markdown Simple formatting is easy for both people and machines to read. Root location The file lives at yourdomain.com/llms.txt. A Mishawaka physical therapy practice publishes an llms.txt file that summarizes its specialties, lists its two clinic locations, links to each treatment page with a one-line description, and points to its insurance and new patient pages. The file takes an afternoon to write and gives AI tools a clean overview of the practice alongside its schema markup and Google Business Profile . The practice updates the file whenever it adds a service or location, keeping it in step with its sitemap. Getting Started With llms.txt Write a short description of your business the way you would explain it to a new customer: what you do, who you serve, and which towns or counties you cover. That paragraph becomes the top of your file. Next, list your most important pages under clear headings such as Services, Locations, Resources, and Contact, with a one-line description for each. Save the file as llms.txt, upload it to the root of your website, and visit yourdomain.com/llms.txt to confirm it loads. Review it whenever your services or pages change. Quick Wins to Improve Your llms.txt File Write a clear one-paragraph summary of your business List your core service pages with short descriptions Include service area and location pages Link to your contact and booking pages Update the file whenever you add or remove key pages Proposed standard. Support varies across AI tools; treat llms.txt as a helpful extra. Accuracy. Keep details identical to your website and Google Business Profile. Brevity. Link to your best pages rather than every page on the site. Foundations first. Clear content, schema, and robots.txt access matter more. No. It is an optional, proposed standard that some websites add to help AI tools understand them. Does Google use llms.txt? Google has not announced support for llms.txt. Its AI features rely on its search index, structured data, and page content. Is llms.txt the same as robots.txt? No. robots.txt sets crawling rules. llms.txt summarizes your site and points to important pages. How long should llms.txt be? Most small business files are short, often a summary and a few dozen links. Does Favze have an llms.txt file? Yes. Favze publishes one at favze.com/llms.txt as

d: The local pack is the map and three business listings at the top of local Google searches. Learn how it ranks businesses and how to earn a spot in Northern Indiana.

b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Local Pack: The map and set of three business listings that Google shows near the top of results for local searches. The local pack, often called the map pack or 3-pack, is the block of three business listings and a map that Google places near the top of results when a search has local intent. Searches like "roofer near me," "coffee shop Warsaw ," or "auto repair Elkhart " trigger it. Each listing comes from a Google Business Profile and shows the business name, rating, review count, category, hours, and quick buttons for calling, directions, or visiting the website. Tapping "More places" opens the full list in Google Maps. Why Local Pack Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses The local pack sits above most organic results on the page, so the three businesses inside it collect a large share of the attention and calls. For service businesses and shops across Northern Indiana and Michiana , earning a spot here is often the single biggest step toward steady local leads. Because results change with the searcher's location, a business can rank first in Goshen and lower in Bristol . Local SEO focuses on widening the area where you appear in the top three. Relevance Google matches the search to your categories, services, description, and website content. Distance Google considers how close the searcher is to your business location or service area. Prominence Reviews, ratings, links, citations, and overall reputation show Google which businesses people trust most. Engagement Calls, clicks, direction requests, and photo views signal that searchers find your listing useful. A Mishawaka dental office appears in the local pack for searches made near its building but drops out two miles away. After adding detailed service pages to its website, earning steady new reviews, and building consistent citations across local directories, the office starts appearing in the 3-pack for "family dentist" searches across Granger and South Bend . Getting Started With Local Pack Begin by searching your top three services the way customers do, such as "water heater repair near me" or "roofing Mishawaka," from a few different spots around your area. Note which businesses appear in the 3-pack and how many reviews, photos, and services each one lists. That snapshot shows the bar you need to clear. Next, close the biggest gap first. If competitors have far more reviews, launch a simple review request process. If their categories and services are more complete, update your Google Business Profile. If they have dedicated pages for each service and town, add those pages to your website. Recheck the same searches every month so you can see your coverage across Elkhart, St. Joseph, Kosciusko, and nearby counties grow over time. Quick Wins to Improve Your Local Pack Rankings Complete your Google Business Profile with the best primary category and all services Build a website page for each main service and town you serve Earn new reviews every month and reply to each one Get listed consistently in trusted local and industry directories Add photos and posts so your profile shows recent activity Grid tracking. Rankings vary block by block, so track results from several points around your area, not just your office. Proximity. You cannot move your address, so strengthen relevance and prominence to reach searchers farther away. Ads above the pack. Local Services Ads and Google Ads can appear above the pack; pairing them with Local SEO covers both spots. Consistency. Mismatched name, address, or phone details across the web weaken trust signals. What is the difference between the local pack and organic results? The local pack shows Google Business Profiles on a map. Organic results are regular website links below it. Strong local businesses work to appear in both. Can I pay to be in the local pack? t: What Are Google Local Services Ads? Pay-Per-Lead Explained

b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Local Services Ads (LSA): Google ads for service businesses that appear at the very top of results with a Google Guaranteed or Google Screened badge. You pay for each lead, such as a call or message, instead of each click. What Is Local Services Ads? Local Services Ads are a Google ad format for local service businesses such as plumbers, electricians, HVAC companies, roofers, cleaners, lawyers, and many others. They often appear at the very top of search results, above regular ads and the map pack. Businesses pass Google's screening and verification, which can include license, insurance, and background checks depending on the category. Approved businesses can display a Google badge, such as Google Guaranteed or Google Screened, and generally pay per lead, such as a call or message, instead of per click. Why Local Services Ads Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses For a Goshen plumber or an Elkhart roofer, Local Services Ads put a trusted badge, rating, and call button at the top of the page when someone needs help right away. That top position and verification badge build instant trust with homeowners comparing options. The pay-per-lead model also makes costs easier to understand. You pay when a potential customer contacts you through the ad, and you can dispute leads that do not fit Google's valid lead guidelines. How Local Services Ads Works Apply and verify Submit business details, licenses, and insurance, and complete required checks. Set service areas and job types Choose the towns you serve and the jobs you want. Set a weekly budget Control how many leads you can receive each week. Receive leads Customers call or message directly from the ad. Manage reviews and responsiveness Ratings and quick replies influence how often your ad appears. An HVAC company in Elkhart County completes Local Services Ads verification and earns the Google Guaranteed badge. It selects furnace repair, AC repair, and installation jobs across Elkhart, Goshen, Middlebury , and Bristol , and answers every lead within minutes. Within a few weeks, the ads produce steady calls, and the company tracks booked jobs in its CRM to measure the cost per job. Because the company also keeps strong reviews on its Google Business Profile , its ads rank well among competitors, showing how Local Services Ads and Local SEO strengthen each other. Getting Started With Local Services Ads Check whether your business category is eligible for Local Services Ads in your area through Google's Local Services Ads sign-up page. Gather your business license, insurance documents, and owner details before you begin, since verification moves faster with everything ready. Once approved, choose your job types and service areas carefully, set a weekly budget you can comfortably handle, and plan how you will answer leads quickly. Respond to every call and message promptly, mark booked jobs in the dashboard, and ask happy customers for reviews to strengthen your ranking. Quick Wins to Improve Your Local Services Ads Select only the job types you want to book Answer calls and messages as quickly as possible Earn steady reviews to improve ad ranking Dispute leads that fall outside valid lead guidelines Track booked jobs to measure cost per customer Eligibility. Available categories and badges vary by industry and region. Responsiveness. Missed calls and slow replies can reduce how often your ad appears. Verification timing. Background and license checks can take several weeks. Lead quality. Mark lead outcomes so you understand your true cost per job. How much do Local Services Ads cost? You pay per lead, and lead prices vary by industry and location. You control spending through a weekly budget. What is the Google Guaranteed badge? t: What Is a Long-Tail Keyword? Finding Searches Ready to Buy
d: Long-tail keywords are longer, specific search phrases with clear intent. Learn why they convert well and how local businesses find and target them.
h: Long-Tail Keyword Specific search phrases from people who know what they want | What Is Long-Tail Keyword? | Why Long-Tail Keyword Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses | How Long-Tail Keyword Works | A Local Example | Getting Started With Long-Tail Keyword | Quick Wins to Improve Your Long-Tail Targeting | What to Watch For | Long-Tail Keyword FAQ
b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Long-Tail Keyword: A longer, more specific search phrase. These phrases attract fewer searches but come from people who know what they want. What Is Long-Tail Keyword? A long-tail keyword is a longer, more specific search phrase, such as "emergency furnace repair in Goshen on weekends" instead of simply "furnace repair." Each long-tail phrase is searched less often than a broad term, yet together they make up a large share of all searches. The name comes from a chart of search demand: a few broad terms with huge volume form the "head," while thousands of specific phrases with smaller volume form the long "tail." Why Long-Tail Keyword Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Specific searches reveal specific needs. Someone searching "how much does a metal roof cost in Indiana" or "pet-friendly patio restaurant in Mishawaka " knows what they want, which makes them more likely to call, book, or visit. Long-tail phrases are also less competitive. A Northern Indiana business may struggle to rank for "lawyer," yet can earn top positions for "estate planning attorney for farm families in Elkhart County ," reaching exactly the customers it serves best. They matter for AI search too. People ask AI assistants detailed, conversational questions, which are long-tail by nature. Content that answers those specific questions is more likely to be cited. How Long-Tail Keyword Works Specific modifiers Words for location, price, timing, features, or problems narrow the search. Clear intent Detailed phrases show what the searcher wants to do. Lower competition Fewer businesses target each specific phrase. Combined volume Many small phrases add up to substantial traffic. Natural questions Voice and AI searches often use full, conversational sentences. A Warsaw boat dealer competes with large regional dealers for "pontoon boats." It creates pages and articles for specific searches such as "best pontoon boat for Lake Wawasee," "pontoon boat financing Kosciusko County ," and "used tritoon boats near Winona Lake ." Each page attracts modest traffic, yet together they bring steady, highly qualified leads from buyers ready to visit the showroom. Several of those pages also start appearing in AI answers when lake residents ask assistants for boat recommendations. Getting Started With Long-Tail Keyword Collect the exact questions customers ask on the phone, in emails, and during visits. Add phrases from Google's "People also ask" boxes, autocomplete suggestions, and the Queries report in Google Search Console , which often shows long-tail searches you already appear for. Group similar phrases by intent. Some fit an existing service page as a new section or FAQ, while others deserve their own article or location page. Write content that answers each question directly, then track impressions and clicks for those phrases over the following months. Quick Wins to Improve Your Long-Tail Targeting Collect real customer questions from calls and emails Check Search Console for long queries you already appear for Add FAQ sections that answer specific questions Combine services with town names on local pages Write articles for detailed cost and comparison questions One page per phrase. Group closely related phrases on one strong page rather than many thin pages. Zero-volume phrases. Tools may show no volume for phrases real customers still search. Natural writing. Use phrases naturally; awkward repetition hurts readability. Intent fit. Match each phrase to the right page type. How long is a long-tail keyword? Usually three or more words, though specificity matters more than length. Do long-tail keywords convert better? They often do, because specific searches reflect clearer needs and readiness to act. Where do I find long-tail keywords? Google Search Console, autocomplete, "People also ask," customer questions, and keyword research tools. Should every long-tail keyword get its own page? No. Related phrases

t: What Is a Meta Description? Writing Snippets That Get Clicks
d: A meta description is the short summary under your title in search results. Learn how to write meta descriptions that earn clicks for Michiana businesses.
h: Meta Description The short summary that sells your page in search results | What Is Meta Description? | Why Meta Description Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses | How Meta Description Works | A Local Example | Getting Started With Meta Description | Quick Wins to Improve Your Meta Descriptions | What to Watch For | Meta Description FAQ
b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Meta Description: The short summary, about 155 characters, that appears under your page title in search results. A strong description invites more clicks. What Is Meta Description? A meta description is a short summary of a web page written in the page code. Search engines often show it below the title in search results, giving searchers a quick preview of what they will find if they click. Meta descriptions do not directly change rankings, yet they strongly influence clicks. Google displays roughly 150 to 160 characters on desktop, and it may choose different text from the page when it believes another passage better matches the search. Why Meta Description Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses When a Goshen homeowner searches "gutter cleaning near me," every result competes for a single click. A description that names the service, the area, and a clear next step, such as "Fast, insured gutter cleaning across Elkhart County . Free quotes in 24 hours," gives that homeowner a reason to choose you. Strong descriptions also set expectations. Visitors who know what they will find tend to stay longer and contact you more often, which makes every ranking more valuable. How Meta Description Works Summarize the page Describe what the visitor will get in one or two sentences. Match the search Use the words people search so Google can highlight them. Include a call to action Invite the next step: call, book, compare, or learn. Add local detail Name towns or counties on local service pages. Keep it unique Each page gets its own description written for its topic. A Plymouth insurance agency uses the same meta description on every page: "Welcome to our website." It writes unique descriptions for each policy page, such as "Compare home insurance options in Marshall County with a local agent who explains every coverage choice. Get a quote today." The agency's click-through rate from Google rises across its main pages over the following months. The agency also notices that callers mention specific coverage types they read about in the search snippet, which makes first conversations faster and more focused. A few sentences of carefully chosen words now do real sales work before anyone reaches the website. Getting Started With Meta Description Run a quick check of your site with a crawler or your SEO plugin to find pages with missing, duplicate, or very short meta descriptions. Prioritize your homepage, top service pages, and the pages that already receive the most impressions in Google Search Console . Write each description as a short sales message: what the page offers, who it is for, where you serve, and what to do next. Read it aloud to make sure it sounds natural. After publishing, compare click-through rates in Search Console over the following month, and test a new version on any page that still underperforms. Quick Wins to Improve Your Meta Descriptions Write a unique description for every important page Keep descriptions around 150 to 155 characters Include the main service and town name End with a clear next step such as "Get a free quote" Update descriptions when offers or services change Rewrites. Google may show different text; descriptions that closely match the page are used more often. Duplicates. Repeated descriptions make results look alike and lower clicks. Overpromising. Promise only what the page delivers so visitors stay. Special characters. Avoid quotation marks that can cut descriptions short in code. Do meta descriptions affect rankings? Not directly. They influence how many people click your result, which makes your existing rankings more valuable. Why does Google ignore my meta description? Does NAP consistency still matter for SEO? Yes. Consistent business details remain a foundation of local search trust, and they help AI tools describe your business accurately. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): An AI method that first looks up relevant documents, then writes an answer based on them. It helps answers stay current and tied to real sources. What Is Retrieval-Augmented Generation? Retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG, is an AI method that first retrieves relevant information from a set of documents or the web, then uses that information to generate an answer. It combines a search step with a language model's writing ability. RAG helps answers stay current and tied to real sources. Many AI search features, including Google AI Overviews , Perplexity, and ChatGPT search, follow this general approach of retrieving web content before writing a response, often with citations to the sources used. Why Retrieval-Augmented Generation Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses RAG is why your website content matters for AI visibility . When a customer asks an AI assistant about the best home inspector in Elkhart , retrieval systems look for relevant, trustworthy pages. Clear, well-structured content gives those systems something useful to retrieve and cite. Businesses can also use RAG internally. A chatbot built on your own service pages, policies, and FAQs can answer customer questions accurately, because it draws from your approved information rather than general knowledge. RAG also explains why freshness matters. Because many AI systems retrieve content when a question is asked, an updated page can influence AI answers quickly, without waiting for a model to be retrained. How Retrieval-Augmented Generation Works Question A user asks a question. Retrieval The system searches an index of documents or the web for relevant passages. Augmentation The retrieved passages are added to the AI's context. Generation The language model writes an answer based on those passages. Citation Many systems show links to the sources they used. A South Bend credit union builds a website assistant using RAG, connected only to its approved pages on accounts, loans, rates, and branch hours. When members ask about auto loan requirements, the assistant retrieves the relevant page and answers with a link to it. Because it relies on approved content, answers stay accurate when the credit union updates its pages. The same clear, structured pages also help public AI search tools retrieve and cite the credit union's information. Getting Started With Retrieval-Augmented Generation Make your website easy to retrieve from. Break long pages into clear sections with descriptive headings, answer questions directly in the first sentences, add FAQ sections, and keep facts current. Each well-labeled section becomes a passage retrieval systems can use. If you are considering a customer-facing AI assistant, choose a platform that grounds answers in your own content, limit it to approved information, show sources in answers, and route complex questions to a person. RAG systems repeat what they retrieve, so stale pages spread stale facts. Poor structure. Long, unorganized pages are harder to retrieve from. Access. Allow reputable AI crawlers if you want public tools to retrieve your pages. Chatbot limits. Restrict business assistants to verified content. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Robots.txt: A small file at the root of your website that tells search engine and AI bots which areas to visit and which areas to skip. It can also list the address of your sitemap . robots.txt is a plain text file at the root of your website, such as favze.com/robots.txt, that gives instructions to automated crawlers. It tells search engine bots like Googlebot and AI crawlers like GPTBot which sections of your site they may visit. The file uses simple rules: a "User-agent" line names the crawler, and "Allow" or "Disallow" lines list paths. It often also points to your XML sitemap so crawlers find every important page quickly. Why Robots.txt Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses A single wrong line in robots.txt can hide an entire website from Google. Website rebuilds sometimes launch with a "Disallow: /" rule left over from development, and a Mishawaka business can lose its search traffic without realizing why. robots.txt also shapes AI visibility . Businesses that want to appear in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI answers keep the doors open for those crawlers, while still blocking areas such as admin pages, carts, and internal search results. Crawlers check first Well-behaved bots read robots.txt before crawling your site. Rules by crawler You can give different instructions to different bots or one rule set for all. Paths allowed or blocked Disallow lines keep crawlers out of specific folders or pages. Sitemap reference A sitemap line points crawlers to your list of important pages. Crawling, not indexing Blocking a page from crawling does not guarantee it stays out of results; a noindex tag handles that. A Goshen manufacturer relaunches its website, and its leads drop sharply over the next month. A review finds the developer left "Disallow: /" in robots.txt from the staging site. After the rule is removed and the sitemap is resubmitted in Google Search Console , Google recrawls the site and its rankings recover over the following weeks. Getting Started With Robots.txt Visit yourdomain.com/robots.txt in a browser and read it. Confirm there is no rule blocking your whole site, check that your sitemap is listed, and note any blocked folders so you know why each one is there. Then use the robots.txt report in Google Search Console to confirm Google can fetch the file without errors. Decide which AI crawlers you welcome; most local businesses benefit from allowing them so AI tools can recommend their services. Keep a copy of the file before any change and recheck it after every website update or migration. Quick Wins to Improve Your robots.txt Confirm your site is not blocked with "Disallow: /" Add your XML sitemap location to the file Block admin, cart, and internal search pages Decide which AI crawlers you want to allow Recheck the file after every redesign or migration Blocking resources. Blocking CSS or JavaScript can stop Google from rendering pages correctly. Noindex confusion. To remove a page from results, use a noindex tag and let crawlers see it. Public file. Anyone can read robots.txt, so it is not a security tool. Case and paths. Rules are case sensitive and must match your URLs exactly. Does every website need robots.txt? It is strongly recommended. Even a simple file that allows crawling and lists your sitemap helps crawlers. Can robots.txt block AI crawlers? Yes. Many AI companies publish crawler names that respect robots.txt, so you can allow or block each one. Will robots.txt remove a page from Google? Not reliably. Use a noindex tag or remove the page, since blocked pages can still appear if other sites link to them. Where do I edit robots.txt? Many platforms and SEO plugins provide an editor. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Schema Markup: Behind-the-scenes code that labels the details on your page, such as business hours, address, reviews, and FAQs, so search engines and AI tools read them accurately. Schema markup is a standard vocabulary of code, published at schema.org, that labels the information on your web pages. It tells search engines that a number is your phone number, a block of text is your business hours, a list is a set of FAQs, and a star rating belongs to a specific service. Visitors never see schema. It usually sits in the page code as JSON-LD, a small block of structured information. Search engines and AI systems read it to understand your business precisely instead of guessing from the visible text. Why Schema Markup Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Clear schema helps Google show rich results such as FAQ answers, breadcrumbs, and business details, and it helps AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews pull accurate facts about your services and location. For a Warsaw orthopedic clinic or a Goshen bakery, that accuracy turns into trust. Most local competitors have little or no schema, so adding it is one of the clearest technical advantages a Northern Indiana business can gain. Choose the right types LocalBusiness or a more specific type such as Dentist or HVACBusiness, plus Organization, Service, FAQPage, Article, and BreadcrumbList. Add accurate properties Name, address, phone , hours, geo coordinates, areas served, services, and social profiles. Place it on the right pages Business details on the homepage and contact page, Service schema on service pages, FAQPage on FAQ sections. Test it Google's Rich Results Test and the Schema Markup Validator confirm the code reads correctly. Keep it current Update schema whenever hours, services, or contact details change. A South Bend law firm adds LegalService schema with its practice areas, office hours, and attorney names, plus FAQPage schema on its estate planning page. Google begins showing the firm's breadcrumbs and page details in results, and AI assistants describe its practice areas correctly when asked about estate planning attorneys in St. Joseph County . Getting Started With Schema Markup Begin with a LocalBusiness block on your homepage and contact page. Include your exact business name, address, phone number, hours, website, logo, geographic coordinates, and the towns or counties you serve. Choose the most specific type that fits, such as Plumber, Dentist, or AutoRepair, so search engines understand your industry right away. Next, add FAQPage schema to sections that answer real customer questions and BreadcrumbList schema to pages deeper in your site. Run each page through Google's Rich Results Test, fix any warnings, and then watch the Enhancements reports in Google Search Console . Once the foundation is in place, add Service schema to each service page and Article schema to helpful guides, so every important page tells search engines and AI tools exactly what it covers. Quick Wins to Improve Your Schema Markup Add LocalBusiness schema with your exact name, address, phone, and hours Use the most specific business type available for your industry Mark up your FAQ sections with FAQPage schema Add BreadcrumbList schema so search results show clear page paths Validate every page with Google's Rich Results Test Match the page. Schema should describe what visitors can actually see on that page. Real reviews only. Review markup must reflect genuine reviews shown on your site. One source of truth. Keep schema details identical to your Google Business Profile . Rich results vary. Valid schema makes rich results possible; Google decides when to show them. Does schema markup improve rankings? Schema helps search engines understand your content, which supports rich results and accurate AI answers. It works best alongside strong content and local signals. Do I need a developer to add schema? Schema is code

b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Search Intent: The reason behind a search: to learn something, compare options, buy, or find a nearby place. Search intent is the purpose behind a search. Someone typing "how to fix a leaky faucet" wants to learn. Someone typing "best plumbers Elkhart " wants to compare. Someone typing "emergency plumber near me" wants to hire right now. Marketers usually group intent into four types: informational (learn), navigational (find a specific site or brand), commercial (research options), and transactional (buy, book, or call). Local searches add another layer: the searcher wants something nearby. Why Search Intent Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Google ranks pages that satisfy the intent behind a search. A service page will struggle to rank for a how-to question, and a blog post will struggle for "near me" searches. Matching the right page type to each search is how Northern Indiana businesses capture customers at every stage. Intent also guides ads. Paid search budgets go furthest on high-intent searches like "furnace repair Goshen ," where people are ready to call. Informational Guides, FAQs, and articles answer questions and build trust early. Commercial Comparison pages, reviews, pricing guides, and case examples help buyers choose. Transactional Service pages, booking pages, and landing pages make it easy to call, book, or buy. Local Location pages and a strong Google Business Profile serve "near me" and town-based searches. A Mishawaka roofing company notices it ranks for "how long does a roof last" but gets few calls. It adds a clear "Roof Replacement in St. Joseph County " service page with pricing ranges, financing details, photos, and a call button, and links to it from the article. The article keeps educating homeowners, and the new page captures people who are ready to hire. Getting Started With Search Intent Make a list of the twenty searches you most want to be found for. Search each one and write down what kind of page appears at the top: a service page, a list of businesses, a how-to article, a map pack, or a product page. That tells you the intent Google has already identified for each search. Next, match each search to one page on your site. Where you have a gap, create the page type Google prefers. Add clear calls to action to service pages, helpful internal links from articles to services, and town names to pages built for local searches across Elkhart, St. Joseph, and Kosciusko counties. Review the list every quarter, since search results evolve as customer behavior changes. Some searches serve several intents; cover the main one first. Shifting results. Intent can change over time, so recheck results for key terms. One page, one job. Pages that try to serve every intent often serve none well. Measure by action. Track calls and form fills, not just traffic, for transactional pages. How do I find the intent of a keyword? Search it and study the top results. The page types Google shows reveal what most searchers want. Which intent brings the most customers? Transactional and local searches convert fastest, while informational content builds trust and future demand. Can one page rank for several keywords? Yes. A page often ranks for many related searches that share the same intent, such as "water heater repair" and "water heater not working." Searches with different intent usually need separate pages. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary List Segmentation: Dividing your contacts into smaller groups by details such as location, interest, or purchase history so every message fits its audience. What Is List Segmentation? Segmentation is the practice of dividing your audience into smaller groups based on shared characteristics, so each group receives messages that fit them. Segments can be built for email, SMS, ads, and even website content. Common segment types include location, customer status (new, repeat, or past), service interest, purchase history, engagement level, and stage in the buying journey. A CRM or email platform keeps track of these details and builds segments automatically. Why List Segmentation Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses One message for everyone usually fits no one perfectly. A Warsaw lawn care company sending a spring aeration offer to commercial accounts, new homeowners, and longtime customers alike misses the chance to speak to each group's real needs. Segmented messages tend to earn more opens, clicks, and sales, and fewer unsubscribes. For local businesses with modest lists, relevance is one of the most affordable ways to grow results. How List Segmentation Works Collect useful data Forms, purchases, and service history capture details such as location and interests. Define segments Group contacts by traits that change what they need to hear. Tailor the message Adjust offers, examples, and timing for each segment. Automate updates Segments update as customers take new actions. Compare results Measure performance by segment to find what works best. A Goshen veterinary clinic segments its email list by pet type and last visit date. Dog owners receive reminders about heartworm prevention in spring, cat owners receive indoor wellness tips, and pets overdue for a checkup trigger a friendly reminder with online booking. Appointment bookings from email rise compared with the single monthly newsletter it used to send. The clinic also creates a segment for clients in Elkhart and Middlebury when it opens a second location, inviting them to book at the new office. Getting Started With List Segmentation Start with two or three segments that clearly change your message. For most local businesses, good first choices are current customers versus prospects, service interest, and location. Add a field or tag in your email platform or CRM for each segment, and update signup forms to capture the information, such as "Which service are you interested in?" Send one tailored campaign to each segment, compare results with your usual newsletter, and expand segmentation where it makes the biggest difference. Start small; each segment needs content you can maintain. Bad data. Keep contact details current so segments stay accurate. Privacy. Collect only data you need and use it responsibly. Overlap. Make sure contacts do not receive conflicting messages. How many segments should I start with? Two or three meaningful segments are plenty to begin with. What data do I need for segmentation? Location, service interest, and customer status cover most local business needs. Can I segment social media ads too? Yes. Ad platforms let you target custom audiences, locations, and interests. What is the difference between segmentation and personalization? Segmentation groups people with shared traits. Personalization tailors details for each individual, such as their name or last service date. The two work best together. Which platform should I use for segmentation? b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Sender Reputation: The score mailbox providers like Gmail and Outlook give your sending domain based on how recipients engage with your emails. Strong engagement builds a strong reputation. What Is Sender Reputation? Sender reputation is the trust level mailbox providers such as Gmail, Outlook, and Yahoo assign to your sending domain and IP address. It is based on how recipients interact with your emails and how responsibly you send. Providers look at signals such as spam complaints, bounce rates, spam trap hits, engagement, authentication, and sending consistency. A strong reputation leads to inbox placement; a weak one leads to spam folders or blocked mail. Why Sender Reputation Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Reputation follows your domain everywhere. A Mishawaka restaurant that sends one careless promotion to an old list can see its everyday emails, including reservation confirmations, start landing in spam. A strong reputation makes every message more effective. When customers in Elkhart , St. Joseph, and Kosciusko counties reliably see your emails, newsletters, reminders, and offers all perform better. How Sender Reputation Works Domain reputation Built over time from the engagement and complaints tied to your domain. IP reputation Tied to the server sending your email, often shared through your email platform. Engagement signals Opens, replies, and moving emails out of spam build trust. Negative signals Complaints, bounces, and spam traps lower trust. Consistency Steady, predictable sending patterns look more trustworthy. A Plymouth hardware store imports a list of old customer emails from years ago and sends a large promotion. Bounces and spam complaints spike, and later emails start landing in spam. The store pauses, removes invalid addresses, sends only to recent and engaged customers for several weeks, and gradually adds back others through a re-engagement email. Its reputation recovers and inbox placement improves. The store now adds new contacts only through its in-store signup and website form, with clear permission. Getting Started With Sender Reputation Set up Google Postmaster Tools for your domain to see how Gmail rates your reputation and spam complaint rate . Review your email platform's bounce and complaint reports for recent campaigns. Then protect your reputation with good habits: send only to people who opted in, remove hard bounces immediately, re-engage or remove long-inactive subscribers, authenticate your domain, and keep sending volume steady. If reputation drops, slow down and send only to your most engaged subscribers until it recovers. Quick Wins to Improve Your Sender Reputation Monitor your domain in Google Postmaster Tools Remove hard bounces after every send Send to engaged subscribers first after any problem Authenticate with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Make unsubscribing quick and easy Old lists. Addresses not emailed in years often bounce or hit spam traps. Complaint spikes. Unexpected emails trigger complaints; set clear expectations at signup. Shared IPs. Reputable email platforms manage shared IP quality for you. Recovery takes time. Rebuilding reputation usually takes weeks of careful sending. How do I check my sender reputation? Google Postmaster Tools shows Gmail's view of your domain, and email platforms report bounces and complaints. Can I recover a damaged reputation? Yes, with clean lists, engaged audiences, proper authentication, and steady sending over time. Does my email platform affect reputation? Your domain reputation follows you, while reputable platforms manage strong IP reputation on their side. Does sending from Gmail or Yahoo addresses hurt reputation? Sending marketing email from a free address usually fails authentication checks. Sending from your own domain, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC in place, builds a reputation that belongs to your business. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Sitemap: An XML file, usually at yoursite.com/sitemap.xml, that lists the important pages of your website so search engines can find and index them quickly. Submitting it in Google Search Console and naming it in robots.txt helps new pages get discovered. An XML sitemap is a file that lists the important pages on your website, often with the date each page was last updated. Search engines read it to discover pages and understand which addresses you want indexed. It is different from an HTML sitemap, which is a page of links for human visitors. Most websites have an XML sitemap at an address such as yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml, generated automatically by the website platform or an SEO plugin. Why Sitemap Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Search engines find most pages by following links, but new pages, deep pages, and pages with few links can take a long time to discover. A sitemap helps a South Bend business get new service and location pages noticed faster. Sitemaps also give you insight. When you submit one in Google Search Console, you can see how many listed pages are indexed and spot problems early, such as pages Google chose to leave out. List canonical pages Include the preferred version of every page you want in search. Add last modified dates Accurate dates help crawlers prioritize updated content. Reference it in robots.txt A sitemap line tells all crawlers where to find it. Submit to search engines Add it in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools. Keep it current Update automatically when pages are added, changed, or removed. A Fort Wayne area HVAC company adds twelve new town pages covering communities around Allen and Whitley counties. Getting Started With Sitemap Check whether your site already has a sitemap by visiting yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml or sitemap_index.xml. Most modern platforms create one automatically. b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Smart Bidding: Automated bidding where Google's AI adjusts your bids for every auction to reach a goal such as more conversions or a target cost per acquisition . Smart Bidding is a group of automated bid strategies in Google Ads that use machine learning to set a bid for every individual auction. It aims to get you more conversions or more conversion value based on the goal you choose. The main strategies are Maximize Conversions, Maximize Conversion Value, Target CPA (cost per acquisition), and Target ROAS ( return on ad spend ). Each one reads signals such as device, location, time of day, audience, and search terms to predict which clicks are most likely to convert. Why Smart Bidding Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Manually adjusting bids for every keyword, hour, and device takes hours each week and still misses signals Google can see. Smart Bidding lets a small Elkhart business benefit from the same automation large advertisers use, freeing time for better ads and landing pages. It only works as well as its data. Businesses with accurate conversion tracking , especially tracked calls and booked jobs, give Smart Bidding the signals it needs to find their best customers. Choose a goal Pick conversions or conversion value as the target. Feed conversion data Accurate tracking tells the system which clicks produce results. Learning period The strategy tests and adjusts during its first weeks. Auction-time bids Bids change in real time based on each searcher's signals. Targets guide spend Target CPA or ROAS settings tell Google how much each result is worth. A South Bend law firm uses manual bidding and struggles to keep cost per lead steady. After tracking qualified calls and form fills for a month, it switches to Maximize Conversions, then moves to Target CPA once it has steady conversion history. The system shifts spend toward weekday mornings and mobile searches near the courthouse, where clients most often call. Because the firm also imports which leads become signed cases from its CRM, the system gradually learns to favor searches that bring real clients instead of quick questions. Getting Started With Smart Bidding Confirm your conversion tracking first. Smart Bidding needs reliable data, so make sure calls, forms, and bookings record accurately and that only meaningful actions count as primary conversions. Begin with Maximize Conversions on a campaign with a steady budget, and allow a learning period of a few weeks before judging. Aggressive targets. Targets far below current results can sharply limit traffic. Constant edits. Frequent changes restart the learning period. Is Smart Bidding better than manual bidding? For most accounts with reliable conversion tracking, Smart Bidding performs well because it uses signals manual bidding cannot reach. How long is the learning period? Google typically describes a learning period of roughly one to two weeks, longer for low-volume campaigns. A strategy that aims to get as many conversions as possible at or near the cost per acquisition you set. Does Smart Bidding work with small budgets? t: What Are SPF, DKIM, and DMARC? Email Authentication Explained
d: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are email authentication records that prove your emails are really from you. Learn what each one does and why Gmail and Yahoo require them.
h: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC The three records that prove your emails really come from you | What Is SPF, DKIM, and DMARC? | Why SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses | How SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Works | A Local Example | Getting Started With SPF, DKIM, and DMARC | Quick Wins to Improve Your Email Authentication | What to Watch For | SPF, DKIM, and DMARC FAQ
b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary SPF, DKIM, and DMARC: Three email authentication settings added to your domain. They prove that your emails are genuinely from you, which helps messages reach the inbox. What Is SPF, DKIM, and DMARC? SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are three email authentication standards set up as records in your domain's DNS settings. Together they prove to inbox providers that emails using your domain are legitimate and have not been altered. SPF (Sender Policy Framework) lists the servers allowed to send email for your domain. DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) adds a digital signature to each email. DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) tells providers what to do when an email fails those checks and sends you reports. Why SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses Without authentication, your emails are more likely to land in spam, and scammers can more easily send fake emails that look like they come from your business. That risk matters for any Northern Indiana business sending invoices, appointment reminders, or newsletters. Since 2024, Gmail and Yahoo require authentication for bulk senders, and Gmail asks senders of 5,000 or more daily messages to its users to set up SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. Smaller senders also benefit, since authenticated mail earns more trust. How SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Works SPF A DNS record lists approved sending services, such as your email host and newsletter platform. DKIM Your sending service signs each email, and receivers check the signature against a public key in your DNS. DMARC A DNS policy tells receivers to monitor, quarantine, or reject failing mail and send reports. Alignment DMARC checks that the visible "From" domain matches the authenticated domain. Reporting DMARC reports show who is sending email using your domain. A Goshen insurance agency sends policy reminders through its agency software, newsletters through Mailchimp, and everyday email through Microsoft 365. Only Microsoft 365 is included in its SPF record, so many newsletters fail checks. After updating SPF, enabling DKIM for each service, and adding a DMARC record in monitoring mode, its emails pass authentication and reach more inboxes. After reviewing DMARC reports for a few weeks to confirm every legitimate service passes, the agency strengthens its policy to quarantine, which helps protect clients from spoofed emails. Getting Started With SPF, DKIM, and DMARC List every service that sends email using your domain: your email host, newsletter platform, CRM, booking tools, invoicing software, and website forms. Each one needs to be included in SPF and set up with DKIM. Then check your current records with a free DNS or DMARC lookup tool. Add or update SPF with all services, enable DKIM in each platform, and publish a DMARC record starting with a monitoring policy (p=none). Review DMARC reports, fix any legitimate services that fail, and then move toward a stronger policy over time. Quick Wins to Improve Your Email Authentication List every service that sends email for your domain Combine all senders into one SPF record Turn on DKIM signing in each email platform Publish a DMARC record, starting with monitoring Review DMARC reports before tightening your policy Multiple SPF records. A domain should have only one SPF record; combine services into it. SPF lookup limits. SPF allows up to 10 DNS lookups; too many includes cause failures. Moving too fast. Jumping to a reject policy before fixing all senders can block real email. New tools. Add each new sending service to your records when you adopt it. Yes. They work together, and major inbox providers expect all three from bulk senders. Where do I add these records? In your domain's DNS settings, usually through your domain registrar or hosting provider. What DMARC policy should I start with? b: Resources / Glossaries / Marketing Terms Glossary Title Tag: The clickable headline shown in search results and on your browser tab. It appears as the blue clickable headline in search results, in the browser tab, and often as the headline when a page is shared on social media. It lives in the page code as a short line inside the head section. Search engines treat the title tag as one of the clearest signals of what a page covers. Google sometimes rewrites titles in results, but it uses the title you provide in most cases when it accurately describes the page. Why Title Tag Matters for Northern Indiana & Michiana Businesses The title tag is often the first thing a searcher reads about your business. For a Mishawaka electrician competing against six other companies on the same results page, a title like "Electrician in Mishawaka, IN | Same-Day Service" tells the searcher immediately that this business fits their need. Better titles mean more clicks from the same rankings. Improving the title tags on your key pages is one of the fastest, lowest-cost SEO upgrades a Northern Indiana business can make. Lead with the main topic Put the service or subject people search near the beginning. Add location when local Include the town or region for pages serving local customers. Include a reason to click A benefit, specialty, or offer helps your result stand out. Fit the space Titles around 50 to 60 characters usually display without being cut off. Add your brand Ending with your business name builds recognition. A South Bend bakery's homepage title reads simply "Home." It changes the title to "Custom Cakes & Fresh Bakery in South Bend, IN | Sweet Crumb Bakery." Within weeks, Google Search Console shows more impressions for cake-related searches and a higher click-through rate , because searchers can now see exactly what the bakery offers and where. Getting Started With Title Tag Open Google Search Console and look at the Pages report under Performance. Sort by impressions and find pages that appear often but earn few clicks. Those pages are your best title tag opportunities, since searchers are seeing them and choosing something else. Rewrite each title to name the service, the town, and a clear benefit, then check that every page on your site has a unique title. Your website platform or SEO plugin usually has a dedicated title field for each page. After the change, give Google a few weeks to recrawl and compare the click-through rate for the same period before and after. Quick Wins to Improve Your Title Tags Replace generic titles like "Home" or "Services" with descriptive ones Name the town or region on local service pages Keep each title unique across your site Place the most important words near the beginning Add your business name at the end Truncation. Long titles get cut off; keep the key message in the first 50 characters. Duplicate titles. Pages with identical titles compete with each other. Rewrites. If Google rewrites your title, make it more accurate to the page content. Match the page. A title should describe what the visitor actually finds. Is the title tag the same as the H1? Not always. The title tag appears in search results, and the H1 appears on the page. They often share a topic but can be worded differently. How long should a title tag be? Aim for roughly 50 to 60 characters so it displays fully on most screens. Why does Google change my title? Google may rewrite titles that are too long, too vague, or that do not match the page. A clear, accurate title is usually kept. Should every page include my city? Include the city on pages that serve local customers. Informational articles can focus on the topic instead.
